contents.name: Godunov and Lax–Friedrichs monotonicity under CFL
contents.detail: Section 4.4.4 gives the Godunov monotonicity argument and Lax–Friedrichs derivative conditions; the local examples specialize and verify the full invariant-interval CFL interface.

contents.name: Discrete entropy flux and monotone update proof
contents.detail: Proposition 4.10 derives the max/min entropy flux using isotonicity of the three-point update. The local proof expands both invariant-interval and exterior entropy-level cases.

contents.name: TVD and temporal translation estimates
contents.detail: Lemmas 4.13–4.14 give the stability route used locally; the local proofs do not rely on the source’s unproved Helly extraction.

contents.name: Helly compactness and Theorem 4.19
contents.detail: Theorem 4.19 fixes the piecewise-linear time interpolant and the positive lower Δt/Δx premise. Theorem 4.18 is an L1 BV compactness statement; the complete local rational-point extraction and initial trace are proved in this batch.

contents.name: Global tail estimate in the source’s L1(R) convergence proof
contents.detail: The source uses U0∈L1(R), a global L1 bound and a finite-propagation tail estimate to obtain global L1 convergence. Batch 29 claims only local convergence and separately proves existence for nonintegrable bounded BV data.

source_limits: Droniou Theorem 2.3.9 and ETH Theorem 4.19 support the monotone-scheme proof route but are not used as substitutes for local proofs.
The Droniou convergence proof cites Helly compactness; the assigned rational-point compactness proof and initial trace are written locally.

ETH Theorem 4.19 proves a global L1 conclusion with an initial L1 tail argument and a positive lower time-to-space ratio. Batch 29 claims local strong convergence, retains the ratio premise, and separately constructs the nonintegrable-data branch.
The ETH Helly statement invokes the L1-based BV norm and therefore does not establish the approved nonintegrable bounded-BV case.
The batch-28 weak-limit theorem assumes strong L1loc convergence and local state bounds and concludes only the weak identity; it does not supply entropy admissibility.
